text_blocks.snippet: An I-9 audit, which assesses an employer's compliance with immigration laws regarding employee work authorization, can be triggered by various factors, including complaints from employees, random selection by authorities, and connections to other investigations. Incomplete or improperly filled I-9 forms, missing documents, and employing unauthorized workers are common reasons for audits and potential penalties.
snippet_highlighted_words: complaints from employees, random selection by authorities, and connections to other investigations

text_blocks.snippet: Specific triggers for an I-9 audit include:

list.title: Complaints:
list.snippet: According to legal experts, complaints from current or former employees, or even job candidates, can initiate an audit. These complaints might allege unfair hiring practices, the hiring of undocumented workers, or other I-9 violations.

list.title: Random Selection:
list.snippet: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) may select employers for audits based on random sampling or industry trends, according to legal experts.

list.title: Connections to Other Investigations:
list.snippet: I-9 audits can also arise as a secondary effect of broader federal investigations, such as those involving the Department of Justice or the FBI.

list.title: Incomplete or Incorrect I-9 Forms:
list.snippet: Errors, omissions, or missing information on I-9 forms can be a red flag. This includes missing signatures, incorrect dates, or failing to complete the form within the required timeframe.

list.title: Employing Unauthorized Workers:
list.snippet: Hiring individuals without proper work authorization or using fraudulent documents can lead to severe penalties.

list.title: Missing or Improperly Stored I-9 Records:
list.snippet: Failing to keep I-9 forms organized and accessible can also trigger an audit.

list.title: Stay Compliant:
list.snippet: Regularly auditing your own I-9 forms and practices can help you identify and correct errors before an official audit.

list.title: Respond Promptly:
list.snippet: If you receive a Notice of Inspection from ICE, it's crucial to respond promptly and provide the requested documentation.

list.title: Seek Legal Counsel:
list.snippet: If you are facing an I-9 audit, it's advisable to consult with an immigration attorney or compliance specialist.
